message.reasoning_content:
We need to read the facts and determine which crimes are directly supported.

Facts: Lin borrowed 730k from Ma, used as business capital. In 2012, he mortgaged a house (registered under his son) to Ma. In July/Aug 2013, to get land certificate, he borrowed back the house deed from Ma, lacking funds, he mortgaged the house to a bank loan, and forged a fake house deed to give back to Ma. Ma discovered in 2015.

Thus crimes: forging state documents? The house deed is a property ownership certificate, which is a "不动产登记证书" (real estate ownership certificate). Is that considered a "国家机关证件"? Under Chinese criminal law, "伪造国家机关证件罪" applies to forging certificates issued by state organs. Real estate ownership certificates are issued by real estate registration authority, a state organ, so forging such a certificate could be "伪造国家机关证件罪". Also possibly "诈骗罪" (fraud) because he used the forged deed to obtain loan from bank and to defraud Ma. However the fact only mentions forging and giving fake deed to Ma. The act of mortgaging to bank using the real house (maybe using the real deed) but forging a fake deed to give to Ma. Could be "诈骗" because he obtained loan from bank using the house as collateral, but that is not described as fraudulent to bank; he used the real house as collateral, not fake. The fake deed was given to Ma to hide the fact that he had mortgaged to bank. That could be "诈骗" of Ma (defrauding Ma of his security interest). However the fact says "伪造了假的房产证交还给马某某". So the crime is forging a certificate. The prosecution says "伪造国家机关证件罪". So we list that.

Also possibly "非法占有他人财产罪" (theft) but not indicated. "贷款诈骗罪" maybe but not explicit.

Thus only crime directly supported: 伪造国家机关证件罪.

Thus answer: [罪名]伪造国家机关证件罪<eoa>
